note: THE GRAMMAR OF THE SORTIE DESCRIPTION BLOCK — the twin of the remarks catalogue. `templates` carry the four squadron templates the user photographed on 2026-08-20, verbatim in `canon`, decomposed into ordered profile elements. A PARENTHESIS IN THE PRINTED TEMPLATE MEANS «OPTIONAL», NOT «PRINT THESE BRACKETS» — the sample photos prove it: the canon writes «(ELP)» and the filled sample writes «ELP». So every element with opt:true renders WITHOUT its brackets when it is on, and disappears when it is off. Anything the four photos do not prove carries status:"draft" plus a `why` — the tab shows those as «DRAFT — proposed variant» and never renders them silently.

codes_note: the remarks grammar — desired (MIF) code -> achieved code. «E» is the failing characterisation code of 3-01 §29.

grades.alias_note: the same syllabus calls this band FAIR at PDF p.165 §14c(1) (air sickness, 59%) and ALMOST GOOD at PDF p.163 §14b(3). ALMOST GOOD is treated as canonical, FAIR as its alias.

grades_source: 3-01_2025_ΔΑΕ.pdf §29 (PDF p.50-51), digitized as data/requirements/failure_procedures.json → fail-01. The Greek scale is the printed one; the English words are the block's own vocabulary — ALMOST GOOD and FAIL are printed in the syllabus (PDF p.163 §14b(3)), EXCELLENT / VERY GOOD / GOOD are the translations of Α / ΛΚ / Κ (VERY GOOD is confirmed by the user's solo-clearance sample photo).
solo_forbidden_note: Syllabus PDF p.163 PART IV §14b(6), verbatim: «(a) All kind of STALLS. (b) SPINS (including Spin Prevention) (c) Unusual Attitudes. (d) ELP. (e) Straight in approach. (f) Slow Flight. (g) No Flap Overhead Patterns/ Landings (h) Simulated Lost Wingman Procedures.» — mapped onto the item numbers of each category.

ep_line.label: Emergency procedures line
ep_line.note: «#39. (1) -> (1): FUEL BALANCE, TAD FAIL.» — the EP gradesheet item of the category, then desired code -> achieved code, then the procedures that were drilled. The item NUMBER differs per category (contact 39 · instrument 32 · formation 36 · navigation 24) and is identical for aircraft and F/S.
ep_line.picks_note: the app draws 2 or 3 at random from data/ep_list.json each time, with a reroll; every pick stays individually replaceable.

rules.note: the flight-rule blank in "____ DEP." / "____ RTB" (canon prints VFR/IFR).

to_types.note: the take-off blank. CONTACT/INSTRUMENT/NAVIGATION canon print STATIC; the FORMATION canon leaves it blank («____ TO») and the syllabus makes INTERVAL the normal formation departure (F41XX §1: T/O interval except two demo flights).

fl_blocks.note: the altitude block. CONTACT canon prints FL100-200, FORMATION F100-200, INSTRUMENT F200-220; the FAIL sample photo writes F100-F200 — all three spellings are offered verbatim, free text stays open.

gca.note: the GCA blank — the printed grade sheet counts ASR and PAR separately.

approaches.note: grounded in TWO printed sources and nothing else: the six approach counters on the printed INSTRUMENT grade sheet (VOR · TACAN · PAR · ASR · ILS · LOC, Syllabus PDF p.235-238) and INSTRUMENT MIF items 20-27 (VOR/TACAN, ILS, Localizer, GCA ASR, GCA PAR, GCA Gyro Out, Standby Instruments, Circling). RNAV appears in NEITHER source, so it is not offered as a preset — the free-text escape covers it if the squadron flies one.

destinations.note: the «AT (DESTINATION)» blank. The airfields the syllabus names for Phase II instrument work (PART IV section blocks) plus the home base. Free text stays open; "(none)" drops the whole "AT …" fragment, which is what the canon's parentheses mean.

solo_scopes.note: the scope of the solo clearance. Only the first is proven by the sample photo; the other two are proposed.
